allocation.hypothesis: Accounting for correlation as well as volatility beats inverse-vol weighting, which double-counts the risk of clustered names

A sleeve chosen purely for low average correlation to the rest of the sector diversifies a core technology holding better than any return-driven selection; if it STILL tracks QQQ, the sector has no independent corner

benchmarks.hypothesis: Equal-weighting the whole live cross-section is the honest passive baseline for any stock-picking claim

breakout.hypothesis: Multi-month highs with a risk-on regime filter precede continuation

breakout.reason: unfiltered variant whipsawed through bear markets and was dominated by the regime-filtered twin at every entry window

buy_and_hold_companies.hypothesis: Holding the losers is the point: these are the outcomes a survivorship-biased sample never shows

factor.hypothesis: Ranking on benchmark-neutral residual return selects genuinely idiosyncratic winners and yields a portfolio less correlated with owning the sector outright
Requiring agreement across 3/6/12-month horizons removes the lookback-selection degree of freedom and cuts whipsaw, at the cost of late entries
Relaxing consensus to 2 of 3 trades earlier; expected to raise turnover more than return
The low-volatility anomaly survives inside a high-beta sector: lower CAGR, higher Sharpe, shallower drawdown. A clean falsification target either way
Deteriorating participation precedes index-level drawdowns, so a breadth gate exits earlier and whipsaws less than a price-trend gate on the index
Capital-spending cycles rotate between layers of the technology stack with enough persistence to trade, without the single-name concentration that penalises stock-level momentum
Acceleration in published revenue growth precedes revaluation more reliably than the level of growth, which is already discounted

meanrev.hypothesis: Oversold snapback exceeds round-trip costs (expected: no)

meanrev.reason: entry=15 duplicates entry=10 with more trades and worse net Sharpe in shakedown
mechanically duplicates RSI reversion (same oversold-in-uptrend trigger); cost-fragile in shakedown

ml.hypothesis: A shrunk linear feature blend ranks forward returns better than any single momentum feature

riskmanaged.hypothesis: Constant-risk sizing improves compounding vs constant-dollar
Drawdowns cluster; scaling down into them cuts the left tail
Trend gates tail risk, vol targeting smooths the path — complementary overlays
Per-name trend filtering matters more over a wide roster, where many names are in their own bear markets while the index rises

target_holdings.hypothesis: Concentrated rotation among the shortlist beats holding all of it

tsmom.hypothesis: Per-name absolute trend cuts the deep tech drawdowns for a CAGR toll

xsmom.hypothesis: Relative strength persists among tech leaders
Given a wide cross-section, relative-strength selection adds value over equal-weighting the same universe

xsmom.reason: momentum-weighting concentrated ~all P&L in the single hottest name (top_name_share ≈ 1); rank information is already in selection

canonical.no_optimization_clause: The first real run executes exactly the frozen grids. No parameter search, selection, or re-ranking outside them is permitted; walk-forward selection in robustness reporting is diagnostic only and does not alter the frozen specification.
canonical.ranking_criteria: composite score = 2*holdout_sharpe + dev_sharpe + 0.5*min(calmar,3) + stability + (PSR-0.5) - degradation - turnover/concentration/complexity/regime penalties + max_dd; verdict relative to best diversified benchmark score + 0.25 margin (see ranking.py fingerprint)
rejection_criteria: fails to beat the best simple diversified benchmark score by the margin
cost-fragile: base-cost edge collapses under the stressed scenario
>50% of P&L from a single security (concentration penalty)
performance dependent on one calendar year (leave-one-year-out)
bootstrap 90% CI on Sharpe includes zero by a wide margin
requires data that failed the quality gate (assigned Tier C, not run)

securities.name: Dell Technologies

successor.notes: operating business to Verizon; remainder became Altaba (AABA)

securities.name: Broadcom Corporation (legacy)
securities.notes: THE trap in this universe. Avago acquired Broadcom Corp and took the Broadcom NAME, but AVGO's price history is Avago's, starting 2009. A vendor series labelled "Broadcom" therefore skips 1998-2009 entirely and shows none of the dot-com boom and bust this company actually lived through. BRCM and AVGO are separate securities here and are never joined.

successor.notes: split into Viavi (VIAV) and Lumentum (LITE); neither inherits the pre-split history cleanly

securities.name: Nortel Networks

successor.notes: assets to Rackable, which then renamed itself SGI — a recycled symbol, not a continuation
